speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to begin our assessment, have you experienced any fever, chills, or nausea alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted your history of recurrent urinary tract infections; have you noticed any clots in your urine, or is the pain severe enough to cause nausea or vomiting? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine culture.

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis confirms significant hematuria and pyuria, suggesting active inflammation or infection; have you noticed any visible clots in your urine, and is the pain colicky, radiating toward your groin? REQUEST TEST: Renal_and_bladder_ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdomen_pelvis_CT_with_contrast.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Ultrasound findings are consistent with the CT imaging, revealing multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction, hydronephrosis, or renal calculi (stones) were visualized. The kidneys show normal size and echogenicity aside from the cystic changes.
